content:
Want to use Signal on multiple devices at once? The encrypted messaging service is making it easier for users to access the app across different iPhones and other devices.

Signal users can now link another iPhone to their existing Signal account, rather than being limited to using an iPad as a second mobile device.

Alongside today's announcement of Android linking, the company said: "We are also expanding linked device support on iOS, so in addition to the iPads we've always supported, you can now also link iPhones to your Signal account."

When linking an additional iPhone, users can optionally transfer their full message history, as well as media stored within the past 45 days.

Signal said the transfer process uses full end-to-end encryption and the same "link-and-sync" technology used for iPads and desktop devices, including Signal for Mac.

This expanded support is particularly useful for anyone who needs to use two iPhones to separate work and personal matters, or for those who need to test multiple devices.

The move also brings Signal's multi-device experience closer to that of the Apple Messages ecosystem, where users can seamlessly continue conversations across iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Signal for iOS version 8.22 is coming soon to the App Store. Signal also recently rolled out a username feature, allowing users to connect without sharing their phone number.
